title: Alexandria normalized matrix set
description: Stage 04-normalized: derived, non-destructive normalization of per-model tables onto one declared scale, stored as research/<slug>/04-normalized/matrices.json. Models answer a matrix brief on whatever scale they choose; collapsing those onto a common scale and taking a median is a derivation, and a derivation belongs in an artifact with a contract rather than inside hand-written analysis prose. Cell values are NOT stored: the median is computed from the votes at read time, so a value that disagrees with its votes cannot exist.

run_id.description: The run whose outputs were normalized.

responding_model_count.description: Models that returned research output and could therefore have scored any cell. Every cell must account for all of them, as votes plus unrecorded ones.

derivation.description: How votes collapse to a cell value. Median, so a single out-of-family vote cannot drag a cell — and so a median across a genuine disagreement stays visible as a spread rather than being smoothed into consensus.

coverage.description: Which cells carry recorded votes. Partial coverage is legitimate and must be stated; silently publishing a matrix whose votes were never recorded is what this stage exists to prevent.

oneOf.description: Every cell of every matrix carries its per-model votes.
Votes recorded only where the published analysis listed them. The remaining cells' votes exist in the raw responses on the host and have not been promoted.

coverage_note.description: Why coverage is what it is, and what would complete it.

axis_rows.description: What a row is — the quality being scored.

axis_columns.description: What a column is — the genre or technique being scored.

rows.description: The full row vocabulary, in published order. Required under coverage 'complete', where it is what makes completeness checkable rather than asserted.

columns.description: The full column vocabulary, in published order. Required under coverage 'complete'.

scale.description: The common scale every vote is normalized onto. A vote outside it is a validation failure, not a curiosity.

kind.description: sequential: magnitude from a floor. diverging: signed, with a meaningful zero.

native_scales.description: The scales the models actually answered on, before normalization. Recorded because the mapping is the step that can go wrong.

cells.description: Cells with recorded votes. Under coverage 'complete' this is every row x column pair.

votes.description: One vote per model that scored this cell, normalized onto the matrix scale. Models that declined are absent rather than zero — a declined cell is a missing observation, never silence.

votes_attributed.description: Whether votes are recorded in a known model order. False where the source analysis published an unattributed list; the multiset is then all that can be claimed.

models.description: Model ids positionally matching votes. Required in practice whenever votes_attributed is true.

unrecorded_model_count.description: Models that responded to the run but whose vote is absent from this list, for any reason. Every responding model must be accounted for as either a vote or an unrecorded one — a cell that quietly holds fewer votes than the panel is how a two-model interpolation comes to look like a three-model median.

unrecorded_reason.description: Why those votes are absent. Required whenever unrecorded_model_count is above zero, because 'the model declined to score' and 'the analysis did not publish it' are different facts with different repairs.

oneOf.description: The model returned output but did not score this cell. A missing observation, never silence, and never zero.
The source analysis did not publish the vote and did not mark a decline. Whether the model scored it is unknown from the corpus alone; the raw responses on the host would settle it.

published_value.description: The value this cell carries in the published analysis, recorded so validation can confirm the derivation still reproduces it. Not a duplicate of derived data — a cross-reference to a separate artifact, checked like a checksum. A signed zero denotes a half-step: -0 is -0.5, +0 is +0.5.
